column4: STOP: STOP: the engine will not turn by hand. Do not try to free it with the starter. Suspect seizure, hydraulic lock (coolant or fuel in a cylinder) or a jammed coupling; inspect before any further attempt.
CAUTION: Batteries give off explosive gas: no sparks or flames near them; disconnect the negative lead first; wear eye protection.

Discharged or failed battery. Actions: Charge the battery fully and re-test at rest and under load (BCI load test or a conductance tester). / Replace a battery that fails the load test; check the charger/alternator output afterwards.
column5: Battery Council International load-test guide: about 12.4 V at rest ≈ 75 % charge; a sound 12 V battery stays at or above 9.6 V under a load test at about 21 °C (double for 24 V systems).

column4: strongly: Rest voltage below about 75 % charge (BCI)
column5: ((systemVoltage is 12 AND restVoltage < 12.4) OR (systemVoltage is 24 AND restVoltage < 24.8))

column4: strongly: Voltage collapses below the BCI load-test level while cranking
column5: ((systemVoltage is 12 AND crankVoltage < 9.6) OR (systemVoltage is 24 AND crankVoltage < 19.2))

column4: supports: Starter clicks or turns slowly
contradicts: Battery holds its voltage while cranking
column5: ((systemVoltage is 12 AND crankVoltage ≥ 10.5) OR (systemVoltage is 24 AND crankVoltage ≥ 21))

column4: Poor battery or starter cable connection. Actions: Isolate, clean and tighten the battery terminals and the starter main and earth cables. / Measure voltage drop across each cable while cranking (positive and earth paths).
column5: General diesel generator service practice (EmersonEIMS); confirm limits and procedure in the OEM service manual for this engine.

column4: strongly: Corroded, loose or hot terminals
supports: Good battery but weak cranking

Starter motor or solenoid fault. Actions: Check the solenoid supply and the main contacts; bench-test the starter.
column5: General diesel generator service practice (EmersonEIMS); confirm limits and procedure in the OEM service manual for this engine.

Start inhibited: emergency stop, controller or interlock. Actions: Find out why the emergency stop was pressed before releasing it. / Read the controller alarm and event log; check the crank relay output.
column5: General diesel generator service practice (EmersonEIMS); confirm limits and procedure in the OEM service manual for this engine.

column4: Engine seized or hydraulically locked. Actions: Do not crank. Remove injectors to check for liquid in a cylinder; inspect for bearing seizure; check the oil for coolant or fuel.
column5: General diesel generator service practice (EmersonEIMS); confirm limits and procedure in the OEM service manual for this engine.

column4: CAUTION: Diesel under pressure can penetrate skin: never feel for leaks by hand; collect spilled fuel; no flames. Follow the starter duty cycle in the manual (crank, then rest) to avoid burning out the starter.
No fuel or fuel starvation. Actions: Fill the tank; check the supply valve, pick-up, lift pump and water separator. / Replace blocked filters; bleed the system.

Air in the fuel system. Actions: Bleed the low-pressure system; find the air leak (loose fittings, cracked line, filter seal, low tank).

column4: strongly: Air bubbles at the bleed point
supports: No smoke while cranking
Fuel shut-off solenoid or ECM fuel enable not working. Actions: Check the solenoid supply, fuse and relay from the controller; check the solenoid plunger and linkage.

Cranking speed too low to start. Actions: Use the "will not crank / cranks slowly" checks: battery, cables, starter, oil grade for the temperature.
column5: General diesel generator service practice (EmersonEIMS); confirm limits and procedure in the OEM service manual for this engine.

ECM, speed sensor or start permissive fault. Actions: Look up the active code in the Fault Code tab; check the speed sensor gap and wiring, and the ECM supply and earth while cranking.

column4: strongly: Active ECM/controller fault code

Cold start aid not working. Actions: Test the glow plugs or intake heater and their relay/timer; use the OEM-approved cold-start procedure only.

Low compression or injection timing fault. Actions: Compression test per the OEM procedure; check injection timing after any pump or timing work.

STOP: STOP the engine: oil pressure is below the OEM minimum. Running on can destroy the bearings in minutes. Do not restart until the cause is found.
STOP: STOP: knocking with an oil pressure problem points to bearing damage. Do not restart; inspect the bearings and the oil filter for metal.
STOP: STOP: metal or coolant in the oil. Do not run until the source is found (bearings; head gasket, oil cooler or liners).
STOP: STOP: oil level below the low mark. Do not run until topped up to the mark with the correct grade and the leak or consumption is found.
Low oil level (leak or consumption). Actions: Top up with the OEM grade; find external leaks; check consumption (blue smoke, breather).

Sender, wiring or display fault (pressure actually normal). Actions: Confirm with a mechanical gauge before any engine work; check the sender, its wiring and the controller calibration.

excludes: The mechanical gauge also reads low

Fuel dilution of the oil. Actions: Find the fuel leak into the sump (injector, lift pump diaphragm, injection pump seal); change the oil and filter after the repair.

supports: Level above full (fuel adding to the sump)
Coolant in the oil. Actions: Pressure-test the cooling system, oil cooler and head gasket; check liners; change the oil after the repair.
column5: General diesel generator service practice (EmersonEIMS); confirm limits and procedure in the OEM service manual for this engine.

Wrong oil or filter, or filter not primed after a service. Actions: Check the filter part number and that the correct grade was used; prime the filter per the manual.
column5: General diesel generator service practice (EmersonEIMS); confirm limits and procedure in the OEM service manual for this engine.

Worn or damaged bearings. Actions: Do not run. Drop the sump, inspect main and big-end bearings and journals; measure clearances.

Oil pump, pick-up or relief valve fault. Actions: Inspect the pick-up screen, pump and pressure relief valve per the manual.

column4: STOP: Take the load off and STOP the engine: coolant above the OEM alarm. Running on can warp the head and seize pistons. Never pour cold water into a hot engine.
STOP: STOP: combustion gas in the coolant suggests a head gasket, cracked head or liner. Do not keep topping up and running.
CAUTION: Do not open the radiator or expansion-tank cap while hot: coolant under pressure scalds. Let the engine cool first.
Low coolant / leak. Actions: When cold, top up with the correct coolant mix; pressure-test for leaks (hoses, radiator, water pump seal).
column5: General diesel generator service practice (EmersonEIMS); confirm limits and procedure in the OEM service manual for this engine.

column4: strongly: Coolant low
excludes: Coolant at the correct level
Head gasket, cracked head or liner. Actions: Combustion-gas (block) test; pressure test; inspect the head and liners.
column5: General diesel generator service practice (EmersonEIMS); confirm limits and procedure in the OEM service manual for this engine.

column4: strongly: Combustion gas in the coolant
contradicts: No gas in the coolant
Fan or water-pump belt. Actions: Isolate the set, then replace or tension the belt to the OEM figure.
column5: General diesel generator service practice (EmersonEIMS); confirm limits and procedure in the OEM service manual for this engine.

column4: strongly: Belt slack, glazed or broken
excludes: Belt correct
Blocked radiator. Actions: Clean the core from the fan side outwards with low-pressure air or water; check internal blockage by temperature drop across the core.
column5: General diesel generator service practice (EmersonEIMS); confirm limits and procedure in the OEM service manual for this engine.

column4: strongly: Radiator core dirty or blocked
excludes: Radiator clean
Hot air recirculation or restricted room airflow. Actions: Clear the inlet and outlet; duct the radiator discharge outside; check louvres open.
column5: General diesel generator service practice (EmersonEIMS); confirm limits and procedure in the OEM service manual for this engine.

column4: strongly: Room or canopy airflow problem
excludes: Free airflow
Overload. Actions: Reduce load to within the rating at site conditions (altitude and temperature derating).
column5: General diesel generator service practice (EmersonEIMS); confirm limits and procedure in the OEM service manual for this engine.

contradicts: Load well within the rating
Thermostat stuck closed. Actions: Replace the thermostat with the OEM rating.
column5: General diesel generator service practice (EmersonEIMS); confirm limits and procedure in the OEM service manual for this engine.

excludes: Thermostat opens correctly
Temperature sender or display fault. Actions: Check the sender and wiring; do not ignore a real overheat to "fix" a sender.
